title.raw: 卷一百三十三 列傳第八十三: 李晟 Volume 133 Biographies 83: Li Cheng

sentences.zh: 徐浩徐浩，字季海，越州人。

translations.literal: Xu Hao—Xu Hao, courtesy name Jihai, a native of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hao, whose courtesy name was Jihai, was a native of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 父嶠，官至洛州刺史。

translations.literal: His father was Qiao, who reached the office of governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu Qiao served as governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 浩少舉明經，工草隸，以文學為張說所器重，調授魯山主簿。

translations.literal: In his youth Hao passed the Mingjing examination, excelled at cursive and clerical script, and because of his literary talent was highly regarded by Zhang Yue; he was appointed by transfer as chief clerk of Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Xu Hao passed the Mingjing examination and was skilled in cursive and clerical calligraphy. Zhang Yue valued his literary gifts and had him appointed chief clerk of Lushan.

sentences.zh: 說薦為麗正殿校理，三遷右拾遺，仍為校理。

translations.literal: Yue recommended him as collator of the Lizheng Hall; after three promotions he became Right Reminder, while still serving as collator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue recommended him as a collator in the Lizheng Hall; after three promotions he became a Right Reminder while continuing as collator.

sentences.zh: 幽州節度使張守珪奏在幕府，改監察御史。

translations.literal: Youzhou military commissioner Zhang Shougui reported that he was in his staff office, and his post was changed to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou military commissioner Zhang Shougui had him serve on his staff, after which he was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，授京兆司錄，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; when the mourning period ended he was appointed recorder of Jingzhao, then left office because of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, then was appointed recorder of the Jingzhao circuit before resigning to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 數年，調授河南司錄，歷河陽令，以善政稱。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred and appointed recorder of Henan, served as magistrate of Heyang, and was known for good government.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he became recorder of Henan and then magistrate of Heyang, where he earned a reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 拜太子司議郎，遷金部員外郎，歷憲部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman for discussion in the heir apparent's household, promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and served as director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was named gentleman for discussion in the crown prince's household, promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and served as a director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，出為襄陽太守、本郡防禦使，賜以金紫之服。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he went out as administrator of Xiangyang and defensive commissioner of that prefecture, and was granted the gold-and-purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Xu Hao was sent out as administrator of Xiangyang and defensive commissioner of the prefecture, with the grant of gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，召拜中書舍人，時天下事殷，詔令多出于浩。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, he was summoned and appointed drafting secretary in the Secretariat; at that time business in the realm was heavy, and many edicts issued from Hao's hand.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong acceded, Xu Hao was recalled as a drafting secretary of the Secretariat; with the empire in crisis, many of the court's edicts came from his pen.

sentences.zh: 浩屬詞贍給，又工楷隸，肅宗悅其能，加兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Hao's compositions were rich and fluent, and he was also skilled in regular and clerical script; Suzong was pleased with his ability and additionally made him concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hao wrote with fluent abundance and was also accomplished in regular and clerical calligraphy; Emperor Suzong delighted in his talents and additionally appointed him concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 玄宗傳位誥冊，皆浩為之，參兩宮文翰，寵遇罕與為比。

translations.literal: The abdication proclamations of transfer of the throne for Emperor Xuanzong were all composed by Hao; he took part in the literary affairs of both palaces, and favor shown him was rarely matched.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted all the abdication documents for Emperor Xuanzong's transfer of the throne and handled literary matters for both the retired and reigning courts—favor seldom rivaled.

sentences.zh: 除國子祭酒，坐事貶廬州長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed chancellor of the Directorate of Education, but because of an offense was demoted to chief administrator of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chancellor of the Directorate of Education but was later demoted to chief administrator of Luzhou for an offense.

sentences.zh: 代宗征拜中書舍人、集賢殿學士，尋遷工部侍郎、嶺南節度觀察使、兼御史大夫，又為吏部侍郎、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong summoned him and appointed drafting secretary and academician of the Jixian Hall; soon he was promoted to vice minister of Works, military commissioner and observation commissioner of Lingnan, and concurrent chief censor, and again served as vice minister of Personnel and academician of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong recalled him as drafting secretary and Jixian Hall academician, then soon promoted him to vice minister of Works, military commissioner and observation commissioner of Lingnan with concurrent rank as chief censor, and later as vice minister of Personnel and Jixian academician again.

sentences.zh: 坐以妾弟冒選，托侍郎薛邕註授京尉，為御史大夫李棲筠所彈，坐貶明州別駕。

translations.literal: He was punished because his younger brother by a concubine improperly obtained selection, entrusting Vice Minister Xue Yong to register and appoint him as a capital district assistant; he was impeached by chief censor Li Qiyun and demoted to vice-prefect of Mingzhou for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached by chief censor Li Qiyun and demoted to vice-prefect of Mingzhou for helping a half-brother secure an illicit appointment as a capital bailiff through Vice Minister Xue Yong.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，征拜彭王傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, he was summoned and appointed tutor to the Prince of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong acceded, Xu Hao was recalled and appointed tutor to the Prince of Peng.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，以疾卒，年八十，贈太子少師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he died of illness at age eighty, and was posthumously granted the title of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the third year of Jianzhong at the age of eighty and was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，浩以文雅稱；

translations.literal: At first Hao was known for literary refinement;
translations.idiomatic: At first Xu Hao was known for literary refinement;

sentences.zh: 及授廣州，典選部，多積貨財，又嬖其妾侯莫陳氏，頗幹政事，為時論所貶。

translations.literal: but after he was assigned to Guangzhou and presided over the selection bureau, he amassed much wealth, and moreover favored his concubine Lady Houmochen, who meddled considerably in government affairs, for which he was criticized by public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: but after he was posted to Guangzhou and headed the selection bureau, he amassed considerable wealth, and his favored concubine Lady Houmochen meddled in affairs of state—conduct for which contemporaries condemned him.

sentences.zh: 趙涓趙涓，冀州人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Juan—Zhao Juan was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan was a native of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有文學。

translations.literal: In his youth he had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He showed literary talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，舉進士，補郾城尉，累授監察御史、右司員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed bailiff of Yancheng, and after successive appointments became investigating censor and vice director in the Right Office of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed bailiff of Yancheng, later rising to investigating censor and vice director in the Right Office of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 河南副元帥王縉奏充判官，授檢校兵部郎中、兼侍御史，遷給事中、太常少卿，出為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Henan deputy commander-in-chief Wang Jin memorialized that he should serve as administrative aide; he was appointed acting director in the Ministry of War and concurrent attendant censor, promoted to supervising secretary and vice minister of Rites, and went out as prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Henan deputy commander Wang Jin had him serve as administrative aide; he was made acting director in the Ministry of War with concurrent rank as attendant censor, then promoted to supervising secretary and vice minister of Rites before being sent out as prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，涓為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongtai era Juan was an investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongtai era Zhao Juan was an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時禁中失火，燒屋室數十間，火發處與東宮稍近，代宗深疑之，涓為巡使，俾令即訊。

translations.literal: At that time a fire broke out in the inner palace and burned several dozen rooms; the place where the fire started was rather close to the Eastern Palace, and Emperor Daizong was deeply suspicious. Juan served as inspection commissioner and was ordered to investigate immediately.
translations.idiomatic: When a fire broke out in the inner palace and destroyed several dozen rooms near the Eastern Palace, Emperor Daizong grew deeply suspicious and appointed Zhao Juan inspection commissioner with orders to investigate at once.

sentences.zh: 涓周歷需囿，按據跡狀，乃上直中官遺火所致也，推鞫明審，頗盡事情。

translations.literal: Juan went all around the palace grounds, followed the traces and evidence, and reported that it had been caused by a eunuch on palace duty who had left a fire unattended; his investigation and interrogation were clear and thorough, and he largely got to the bottom of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan searched the palace grounds, followed the evidence, and determined that a eunuch on duty had left a fire unattended; his investigation was thorough and brought the affair to light.

sentences.zh: 既奏，代宗稱賞焉。

translations.literal: After he submitted his report, Daizong praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted his findings, Emperor Daizong praised him.

sentences.zh: 德宗時在東宮，常感涓之究理詳細，及刺衢州，年考既深，又與觀察使韓滉不相得，滉奏免涓官，德宗見其名，謂宰臣曰：「豈非永泰初御史趙涓乎？」

translations.literal: At that time Dezong was in the Eastern Palace and had often been impressed by Juan's detailed thoroughness in getting to the bottom of things. When Juan was prefect of Quzhou, his annual evaluation had already been long in arrears, and he also did not get along with observation commissioner Han Huang, who memorialized to dismiss Juan from office. Dezong saw his name and said to the chief ministers, "Is this not investigating censor Zhao Juan from the beginning of Yongtai?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Dezong had long admired Zhao Juan's thorough investigations. Later, as prefect of Quzhou, Zhao Juan's annual evaluation was overdue and he clashed with observation commissioner Han Huang, who memorialized for his dismissal. When Dezong saw the name he asked his chief ministers, "Is this not investigating censor Zhao Juan from the beginning of Yongtai?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「然。」

translations.literal: They replied, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "It is."

sentences.zh: 即拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He immediately appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed Zhao Juan Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 無何，知吏部選，扈從梁州。

translations.literal: Before long he was placed in charge of selections in the Ministry of Personnel and accompanied the court to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was placed in charge of personnel selections and accompanied the court to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 興元元年卒，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan he died, and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously honored as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子 博宣子博宣，登進士第，文章俊拔，性率多酒。

translations.literal: His son Bozhuan—Bozhuan passed the jinshi examination; his essays were outstanding, and by nature he was frank and fond of wine.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Bozhuan passed the jinshi examination; his writing was brilliant, but he was frank by nature and drank heavily.

sentences.zh: 陳許節度使曲環辟為從事，賓筵之間多所忽略，環不能容。

translations.literal: Chenxu military commissioner Qu Huan recruited him as an aide; at banquets he often neglected propriety, and Huan could not tolerate it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxu military commissioner Qu Huan recruited him as an aide, but Zhao Bozhuan often neglected propriety at banquets, which Qu Huan could not abide.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方討淮、蔡，環誣奏博宣受吳少誠賂為反間，又妄說國家休咎，扇惑軍情。

translations.literal: The court was then campaigning against Huai and Cai; Huan falsely memorialized that Bozhuan had accepted bribes from Wu Shaocheng to act as a spy, and also recklessly spoke of the state's fortunes and misfortunes, stirring up military sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was campaigning against Huai and Cai, Qu Huan falsely accused Zhao Bozhuan of taking bribes from Wu Shaocheng to spy for the enemy and of spreading reckless talk about the state's fortunes to stir up the troops.

sentences.zh: 時博宣權知舞陽縣事，詔令環決杖四十，流於康州，人皆以為枉。

translations.literal: At that time Bozhuan was acting in the affairs of Wuyang county; an edict ordered Huan to impose forty strokes of the staff and exile him to Kangzhou, and people all considered it a wrongful punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bozhuan was then acting magistrate of Wuyang; the court ordered Qu Huan to impose forty strokes of the staff and exile him to Kangzhou—a punishment widely regarded as unjust.

sentences.zh: 先是，侍御史盧南史坐事貶信州員外司馬，至郡，準例得廳吏一人，每月請紙筆錢，前後五年，計錢一千貫。

translations.literal: Earlier, attendant censor Lu Nanshi was punished for an offense and demoted to supernumerary vice prefect of Xinzhou; on reaching the prefecture, according to precedent he was entitled to one office clerk, who each month requested paper-and-brush money—for five years in all, amounting to one thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, attendant censor Lu Nanshi had been demoted to supernumerary vice prefect of Xinzhou; on arrival he was entitled under precedent to one office clerk, who for five years had collected paper-and-brush allowances totaling one thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 南史以官閑冗，放吏歸，納其紙筆錢六十余千。

translations.literal: Nanshi, finding his post idle and superfluous, released the clerk to return home and took in more than sixty thousand of the paper-and-brush money.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his post largely idle, Lu Nanshi released the clerk and retained more than sixty thousand in paper-and-brush allowances.

sentences.zh: 刺史姚驥劾奏南史，以為贓，又劾南史買鉛燒黃丹。

translations.literal: Prefect Yao Ji impeached and memorialized against Nanshi, treating this as embezzlement, and also impeached Nanshi for buying lead and smelting yellow cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yao Ji impeached Lu Nanshi for embezzlement and also accused him of buying lead to smelt yellow cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣監察御史鄭楚相、刑部員外郎裴澥、大理評事陳正儀充三司使，同往按鞫。

translations.literal: Dezong dispatched investigating censor Zheng Chuxiang, vice director in the Ministry of Justice Pei Xie, and reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Zhengyi to serve as the three-commissioners mission and go together to investigate and interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong dispatched investigating censor Zheng Chuxiang, vice director in the Ministry of Justice Pei Xie, and Court of Judicial Review reviewer Chen Zhengyi as a three-commissioner team to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 將行，並召於延英，謂之曰：「卿等必須詳審，無令漏罪銜冤。」

translations.literal: Before they set out, he summoned them all to Yanying and said to them, "You must investigate in detail and not let crimes go unpunished or allow the wronged to bear injustice."
translations.idiomatic: Before they departed he summoned them to Yanying Hall and said, "You must investigate thoroughly—let no crime go unpunished and no innocent man bear injustice."

sentences.zh: 三人將退，裴澥獨留，奏曰：「臣按姚驥奏狀，稱南史取廳吏紙筆錢計贓六十余貫，雖於公法有違，量事且非巨蠹。」

translations.literal: The three were about to withdraw when Pei Xie alone remained and memorialized, "Your servant has examined Prefect Yao Ji's memorial, which states that Nanshi took the office clerk's paper-and-brush money, counting it as embezzlement of more than sixty strings; although this violates public law, measured by the matter it is not a great corruption."
translations.idiomatic: As the three were leaving, Pei Xie alone remained and said, "I have reviewed Prefect Yao Ji's memorial. Lu Nanshi's retention of more than sixty strings in paper-and-brush money violates the law, but by any measure it is not a grave corruption."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此事亦未為甚，未知燒鉛何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This matter also is not very serious; I do not know how the smelting of lead stands?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That offense is not grave either. What of the charge of smelting lead?"

sentences.zh: 澥曰：「燒鉛為丹，格令不禁。

translations.literal: Xie said, "Smelting lead to make cinnabar is not forbidden by statute.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xie said, "Smelting lead into cinnabar is not forbidden by statute.

sentences.zh: 準天寶十三載敕，鉛、銅、錫不許私家買賣貨易，蓋防私鑄錢，本亦不言燒鉛為丹。

translations.literal: According to the edict of the thirteenth year of Tianbao, lead, copper, and tin were not permitted to be bought, sold, or traded by private persons—this was to guard against private coining, and originally it also did not speak of smelting lead to make cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: The edict of the thirteenth year of Tianbao forbade private trade in lead, copper, and tin to prevent illicit coining; it said nothing about smelting lead into cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 南史違敕買鉛，不得無罪。

translations.literal: Nanshi violated the edict in buying lead and cannot be without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Nanshi did violate the edict by purchasing lead and cannot be held entirely blameless.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下自登寶位，及天寶、大歷以來，未曾降三司使至江南；

translations.literal: Your servant submits that since Your Majesty ascended the throne, and from the Tianbao and Dali eras until now, a three-commissioners mission has never been sent down to the Jiangnan region;
translations.idiomatic: Yet since Your Majesty's accession, and indeed since the Tianbao and Dali eras, no three-commissioner mission has ever been sent to the Jiangnan region;

sentences.zh: 今忽錄此小事，令三司使往，非唯損耗州縣，亦恐遠處聞之，各懷憂懼。

translations.literal: now suddenly to take note of this small matter and send a three-commissioners mission will not only drain the prefectures and counties but also, I fear, cause distant places on hearing of it each to harbor worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: to dispatch such a mission over this trifling matter will not only burden the prefectures and counties but may alarm distant regions when they hear of it.

sentences.zh: 臣聞開元中張九齡為五嶺按察使，有錄事參軍告齡非法，朝廷止令大理評事往按。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in the Kaiyuan era Zhang Jiuling served as inspection commissioner of the Five Ridges; when a recording secretary reported Jiuling's illegal acts, the court only sent a reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that in the Kaiyuan era, when a recording secretary reported illegal conduct by Zhang Jiuling, inspection commissioner of the Five Ridges, the court sent only a Court of Judicial Review reviewer to investigate.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，鄂嶽觀察使吳仲孺與轉運使判官劉長卿紛競，仲孺奏長卿犯贓二十萬貫，時止差監察御史苗伾就推。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, E-Yue observation commissioner Wu Zhongru competed with transport commissioner aide Liu Changqing; Zhongru memorialized that Changqing had committed embezzlement of two hundred thousand strings, and at the time only investigating censor Miao Pi was sent to conduct the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, when E-Yue observation commissioner Wu Zhongru accused transport aide Liu Changqing of embezzling two hundred thousand strings amid their rivalry, the court sent only investigating censor Miao Pi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 今姚驥所奏事狀無多，臣堪任此行，即請獨往，恐不須三司並行為使。」

translations.literal: The matters in Prefect Yao Ji's present memorial are not many; your servant is fit for this mission and requests to go alone—I fear it is not necessary for all three commissioners to go together as envoys."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yao Ji's charges are slight; I am fit for this mission and ask to go alone—there is no need for all three commissioners to travel together."

sentences.zh: 德宗忻然曰：「卿言是矣。」

translations.literal: Dezong said with pleasure, "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong said with pleasure, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 乃復召楚相、正儀與澥俱坐，謂之曰：「朕懵於理道，處事未精，適見裴澥所奏，深協事宜，亦不用三人總去，但行首一人行可也，卿等使宣付宰臣改敕。」

translations.literal: He then summoned Chuxiang, Zhengyi, and Xie to sit together again and said to them, "We are dull in the Way of governance and handle affairs without refinement; just now seeing Pei Xie's memorial, it deeply accords with what is fitting. There is also no need for all three to go—only the chief commissioner need go. You shall announce this and have the chief ministers revise the edict."
translations.idiomatic: He then recalled Zheng Chuxiang and Chen Zhengyi and said, "I am still unskilled in governance; Pei Xie's memorial accords with what is fitting. All three of you need not go—only the lead commissioner. Announce this and have the chief ministers revise the edict.

sentences.zh: 德宗不務大體，以察為明，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Dezong did not attend to the larger pattern and took minute scrutiny for clarity—all were cases of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong neglected larger principles and mistook minute scrutiny for wisdom—this was typical of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 而博宣、南史坐誣枉擯逐，賴裴澥悟主，南史不至深罪，後得召還。

translations.literal: Bozhuan and Nanshi suffered wrongful impeachment and banishment; thanks to Pei Xie's enlightening the ruler, Nanshi did not receive a heavy sentence and was later able to be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bozhuan and Lu Nanshi were wrongly impeached and driven out; thanks to Pei Xie's persuasion of the emperor, Lu Nanshi escaped severe punishment and was later recalled.

sentences.zh: 劉太真劉太真，宣州人。

translations.literal: Liu Taizhen—Liu Taizhen was a native of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taizhen was a native of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 涉學，善屬文，少師事詞人蕭穎士。

translations.literal: He had broad learning, was skilled at literary composition, and in his youth studied under the man of letters Xiao Yingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and skilled at composition, he studied in his youth under the poet Xiao Yingshi.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，舉進士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，為淮南節度使陳少遊掌書記，征拜起居郎。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he served as recorder for Huainan military commissioner Chen Shaoyou and was summoned and appointed attendant of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era he served as recorder to Huainan military commissioner Chen Shaoyou before being summoned as attendant of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 累歷臺閣，自中書舍人轉工部、刑部二侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served in the censorate and secretariat, and from drafting secretary was transferred to vice minister of Works and vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the censorate and secretariat, moving from drafting secretary to vice minister of Works and vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 性怯懦詭隨。

translations.literal: By nature he was timid, evasive, and accommodating.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was timid, evasive, and accommodating.

sentences.zh: 及轉禮部侍郎，掌貢舉，宰執姻族，方鎮子弟，先收擢之。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to vice minister of Rites and presided over the civil examinations, he first selected and promoted relatives of chief ministers and sons of regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: As vice minister of Rites presiding over the civil examinations, he favored relatives of chief ministers and sons of regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 又常敘少遊勛績，擬之桓、文，大招物論。

translations.literal: He also often recounted Shaoyou's achievements and compared him to Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi, greatly provoking public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: He also often praised Chen Shaoyou's achievements by comparing him to Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi, provoking widespread criticism.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，貶信州刺史，到州尋卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was demoted to prefect of Xinzhou and died soon after reaching the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was demoted to prefect of Xinzhou and died soon after taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 太真尤長於詩句，每出一篇，人皆諷誦。

translations.literal: Taizhen was especially accomplished in poetic lines; whenever he produced a piece, people all recited and chanted it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taizhen excelled above all at poetry; whenever he published a new piece, people recited it throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 德宗文思俊拔，每有禦制，即命朝臣畢和。

translations.literal: Dezong's literary thought was outstanding; whenever he had an imperial composition, he ordered all the court officials to compose matching poems.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong's literary gifts were outstanding; whenever he composed an imperial poem, he ordered the entire court to write matching verses.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年九月，賜宴曲江亭，帝為詩，序曰：

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan he granted a banquet at Qujiang Pavilion; the emperor composed a poem, and the preface read:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan he held a banquet at Qujiang Pavilion and composed a poem whose preface read:

sentences.zh: 朕在位僅將十載，實賴忠賢左右，克致小康。

translations.literal: We have been on the throne for nearly ten years, and truly rely on loyal and worthy men at our side to achieve a modest peace and prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: I have been on the throne for nearly ten years, and it is truly through loyal and worthy men at my side that we have achieved a modest peace and prosperity.

sentences.zh: 是以擇三令節，錫茲宴賞，俾大夫、卿士得同歡洽也。

translations.literal: Therefore We have chosen the three fine festivals and granted this banquet and reward, so that grand masters and ministers may share in joyous harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have chosen the three fine festivals for this banquet and reward, so that grand masters and ministers may share in joyous harmony.

sentences.zh: 夫共其戚者同其休，有其初者貴其終，咨爾群僚，頒朕不暇，樂而能節，職思其憂，鹹若時則，庶乎理矣。

translations.literal: Those who share in sorrow share in joy; those who have a beginning value the end. We address you, assembled officials: though We distribute Our bounty without cease, rejoice yet with restraint, and in your offices think of what should concern you. If all accord with the season, governance may perhaps be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Those who share sorrow share joy; those who begin well must value the end. I address you, assembled officials: though I grant bounty without cease, rejoice with restraint and in your offices keep duty's cares in mind. If all accord with the season, good governance may be achieved.

sentences.zh: 因重陽之會，聊示所懷。

translations.literal: On the occasion of the Double Ninth Festival, We briefly set forth what is in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of the Double Ninth Festival, I briefly set forth what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: 早衣對庭燎，躬化勤意誠。

translations.literal: Rising early to dress before the court torches, personally transforming with diligent sincerity of purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Rising early to dress before the court torches, I personally lead with diligent and sincere purpose.

sentences.zh: 時此萬樞暇，適與佳節並。

translations.literal: At this time, amid the myriad affairs of state, a moment of leisure coincides with the fine festival.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the myriad affairs of state, a moment of leisure now coincides with this fine festival.

sentences.zh: 曲池絜寒流，芳菊舒金英。

translations.literal: The winding pool holds clear cold currents; fragrant chrysanthemums unfold their golden blooms.
translations.idiomatic: The winding pool holds clear cold currents; fragrant chrysanthemums unfold their golden blooms.

sentences.zh: 乾坤爽氣澄，臺殿秋光清。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are clarified by crisp air; terraces and halls shine with clear autumn light.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are clarified by crisp air; terraces and halls shine with clear autumn light.

sentences.zh: 朝野慶年豐，高會多歡聲。

translations.literal: Court and countryside celebrate a bountiful year; at this lofty gathering many sounds of joy arise.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside celebrate a bountiful year; at this lofty gathering many sounds of joy arise.

sentences.zh: 永懷無荒誡，良士同斯情。

translations.literal: Ever mindful of the admonition against dissipation, worthy men share this feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Ever mindful of the admonition against dissipation, worthy men share this feeling.

sentences.zh: 因詔曰：「卿等重陽會宴，朕想歡洽，欣慰良多，情發於中，因制詩序。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict saying, "You held a Double Ninth gathering and banquet; We think of your joyous harmony and are greatly comforted. Feeling arose from within, and We therefore composed this poem and preface.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "At your Double Ninth gathering I thought of your joyous harmony and was greatly comforted. Feeling arose from within, and I therefore composed this poem and preface.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿等一本，可中書門下簡定文詞士三五十人應制，同用『清』字，明日內於延英門進來。」

translations.literal: Now We grant each of you a copy; the Secretariat and Chancellery may select thirty to fifty men of letters to compose matching poems on imperial command, all using the rhyme word 'clear,' and submit them at Yanying Gate within tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: I now grant each of you a copy. The Secretariat and Chancellery may select thirty to fifty men of letters to compose matching poems on imperial command, all using the rhyme word 'clear,' and submit them at Yanying Gate by tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 宰臣李泌等雖奉詔簡擇，難於取舍，由是百僚皆和。

translations.literal: Chief ministers such as Li Bi, though they received the edict to make selections, found it difficult to choose, and therefore all the officials composed matching poems.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers such as Li Bi, though ordered to make selections, found it difficult to choose, and therefore the entire bureaucracy composed matching poems.

sentences.zh: 上自考其詩，以太真及李紓等四人為上等，鮑防、于邵等四人為次等，張濛、殷亮等二十三人為下等；

translations.literal: The emperor himself examined the poems and ranked Liu Taizhen and Li Shu and four others in the top grade, Bao Fang and Yu Shao and four others in the second grade, and Zhang Meng, Yin Liang, and twenty-three others in the lowest grade;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself graded the poems, ranking Liu Taizhen, Li Shu, and four others in the top grade; Bao Fang, Yu Shao, and four others in the second grade; and Zhang Meng, Yin Liang, and twenty-three others in the lowest grade;

sentences.zh: 而李晟、馬燧、李泌三宰相之詩，不加考第。

translations.literal: but the poems of the three chief ministers Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Li Bi were not given grades.
translations.idiomatic: but the poems of chief ministers Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Li Bi received no grade.

sentences.zh: 初，硃泚、懷光之亂，關輔薦饑，貞元三年以後，仍歲豐稔，人始復生人之樂。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the disorders of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang, the Guanfu region suffered repeated famine; after the third year of Zhenyuan, year after year brought abundant harvests, and people at last recovered the joy of human life.
translations.idiomatic: After the disorders of Zhu Ci and Li Huai Guang, the Guanzhong region had suffered repeated famine; from the third year of Zhenyuan onward harvests were abundant year after year, and people at last recovered the ordinary joys of life.

sentences.zh: 德宗詔曰：「比者卿士內外，朝夕公務，今方隅無事，蒸民小康，其正月晦日、三月三日、九月九日三節日，宜任文武百僚擇勝地追賞。

translations.literal: Dezong issued an edict saying, "Recently officials within and without the court have been occupied morning and evening with public business. Now the four quarters are at peace and the common people enjoy modest prosperity. On the three festivals—the last day of the first month, the third day of the third month, and the ninth day of the ninth month—it is fitting to allow civil and military officials of all ranks to choose scenic places for outings and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong issued an edict: "Officials within and without the court have lately been occupied morning and evening with public business. Now the realm is at peace and the people enjoy modest prosperity. On the three festivals—the last day of the first month, the third day of the third month, and the ninth day of the ninth month—civil and military officials of all ranks may choose scenic places for outings and rewards.

sentences.zh: 每節宰相、常參官共賜錢五百貫文、翰林學士一百貫文，左右神威、神策等十軍各賜五百貫。

translations.literal: On each festival the chief ministers and regular attendees at court are together granted five hundred strings of cash, Hanlin academicians one hundred strings, and each of the ten armies including the Left and Right Shenwei and Shence five hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: On each festival the chief ministers and regular attendees at court are granted five hundred strings of cash together, Hanlin academicians one hundred strings, and each of the ten armies including the Left and Right Shenwei and Shence five hundred strings.

sentences.zh: 金吾英武、威遠及諸衛將軍共賜二百貫，客省奏事共賜一百貫，委度支每節前五日支付，永為常制。」

translations.literal: The Jinwu Yingwu, Weiyuan, and various guard generals are together granted two hundred strings; those who present memorials at the Guest Bureau one hundred strings. The Ministry of Revenue is entrusted to pay five days before each festival; this shall be a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinwu Yingwu, Weiyuan, and guard generals receive two hundred strings together; those who present memorials at the Guest Bureau one hundred strings. The Ministry of Revenue shall pay five days before each festival as a permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 李紓李紓，字仲舒，禮部侍郎希言之子。

translations.literal: Li Shu—Li Shu, courtesy name Zhongshu, was the son of Vice Minister of Rites Li Xiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu, whose courtesy name was Zhongshu, was the son of Vice Minister of Rites Li Xiyan.

sentences.zh: 少有文學。

translations.literal: In his youth he had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He showed literary talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，拜秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era he was appointed collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，吏部侍郎李季卿薦為左補闕，累遷司封員外郎、知制誥，改中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era, Vice Minister of Personnel Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Remonstrator; after successive promotions he became vice director in the Ministry of Rites in charge of edicts and was changed to drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Dali era Vice Minister of Personnel Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Remonstrator; he rose to vice director in the Ministry of Rites in charge of edicts and then became drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋自虢州刺史征拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned from prefect of Guo and appointed vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled from his post as prefect of Guo and appointed vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 德宗居奉天，擇為同州刺史，尋棄州詣梁州行在，拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, he was selected as prefect of Tongzhou; soon he abandoned the prefecture and went to the mobile court at Liangzhou, where he was appointed vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong was at Fengtian, Li Shu was appointed prefect of Tongzhou; he soon abandoned the prefecture and went to the mobile court at Liangzhou, where he was made vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 反正，兼知選事。

translations.literal: After the restoration he was additionally placed in charge of selections.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration he was additionally placed in charge of personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 李懷光誅，河東節度及諸軍會河中，詔往宣勞節度，使還，敷奏合旨，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Li Huai Guang was executed, the Hedong military commission and various armies assembled at Hezhong; an edict sent him to proclaim consolation to the military commission. On his return his memorials accorded with the emperor's intent, and he was appointed vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Huai Guang was executed, when the Hedong military commission and allied armies assembled at Hezhong, Li Shu was sent to proclaim the court's consolation. On his return his memorials pleased the emperor and he was appointed vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 紓通達，善詼諧，好接後進，厚自奉養，鮮華輿馬，以放達蘊藉稱。

translations.literal: Shu was open and penetrating, skilled at wit and humor, fond of receiving younger talents, lavish in his own maintenance, with splendid carriages and horses, and was known for being unrestrained yet refined.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu was open and penetrating, skilled at wit, fond of mentoring younger talents, and lavish in his style of living, with splendid carriages and horses; he was known for being unrestrained yet refined.

sentences.zh: 雖為大官，而佚遊佐宴，不嘗自忘。

translations.literal: Although a high official, he delighted in roaming and assisting at banquets and never forgot himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though a high official, he delighted in leisure, travel, and banquets and never forgot himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗議享武成王不當視文宣廟，奏云：「準開元十九年敕，置齊太公廟，以張良配，太常卿及少卿、丞充三獻官。

translations.literal: He once argued that sacrifices to King Wucheng should not be treated on a par with the temple of King Wenzuan, memorializing, "According to the edict of the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan, a temple to Lord Tai of Qi was established, with Zhang Liang as associate; the Minister of Rites and vice ministers and directors served as the three offering officials.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that sacrifices to King Wucheng should not be treated on a par with the temple of King Wenzuan, memorializing, "According to the edict of the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan, a temple to Lord Tai of Qi was established with Zhang Liang as associate; the Minister of Rites and his vice ministers and directors served as the three offering officials.

sentences.zh: 又按《開元禮》祝文雲『皇帝遣某官昭告於齊太公、漢留侯』。

translations.literal: Moreover, according to the Kaiyuan Rites, the prayer text reads, 'The emperor sends a certain official to proclaim to Lord Tai of Qi and Marquis Liu of Han.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, according to the Kaiyuan Rites, the prayer text reads, 'The emperor sends a certain official to proclaim to Lord Tai of Qi and Marquis Liu of Han.'

sentences.zh: 至上元年，敕追贈太公為武成王，享祭之典，一同文宣王，有司因差太尉充獻官，兼禦署祝板。

translations.literal: Up to the first year of the Shangyuan era, an edict posthumously ennobled Lord Tai as King Wucheng, and the sacrificial rites were made identical to those of King Wenzuan; the responsible offices therefore assigned the Grand Marshal as offering official and also had him sign the imperial prayer board.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan an edict posthumously ennobled Lord Tai as King Wucheng and made his sacrificial rites identical to those of King Wenzuan; the responsible offices therefore assigned the Grand Marshal as offering official and had him sign the imperial prayer board.

sentences.zh: 伏以太公即周之太師，張良即漢之少傅，聖朝列於祀典，已極褒崇；

translations.literal: Your servant submits that Lord Tai was Grand Tutor of Zhou, and Zhang Liang was Junior Tutor of Han; our sage dynasty has placed them in the sacrificial canon, and honor has already reached its utmost;
translations.idiomatic: I submit that Lord Tai was Grand Tutor of Zhou and Zhang Liang was Junior Tutor of Han; our dynasty has placed them in the sacrificial canon with the highest honor;

sentences.zh: 今屈禮於至尊，施敬於臣佐，理或過當，神何敢歆。

translations.literal: Now to bend ritual before the supreme sovereign and show reverence to a ministerial assistant—reason may exceed what is fitting; how would the spirits dare to accept it?
translations.idiomatic: To bend ritual before the supreme sovereign and show reverence to a ministerial assistant exceeds what is fitting—how would the spirits dare to accept such offerings?

sentences.zh: 伏以文宣垂教，百代宗師，五常三綱，非其訓不明，有國有家，非其制不立，故孟軻稱『生人已來，一人而已』。

translations.literal: Your servant submits that King Wenzuan handed down teaching as master for a hundred generations; the five constants and three bonds would not be clear without his instruction, and states and families would not be established without his institutions. Therefore Mencius said, 'Since mankind began, there has been only one such man.'
translations.idiomatic: I submit that King Wenzuan handed down teaching as master for a hundred generations; without his instruction the five constants and three bonds would be unclear, and without his institutions states and families could not stand. Mencius therefore said, 'Since mankind began, there has been only one such man.'

sentences.zh: 由是正素王之位，加先聖之名，樂用宮懸，獻差太尉，尊師崇道，雅合政經。

translations.literal: Hence he was given the position of the uncrowned king, granted the title of prior sage, used palace music with suspended bells, and had the Grand Marshal assigned as offering official—honoring the teacher and exalting the Way, which elegantly accords with the canon of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Hence he was given the position of uncrowned king and the title of prior sage, with palace music and the Grand Marshal as offering official—honoring the teacher and exalting the Way in a manner that elegantly accords with the canon of governance.

sentences.zh: 且太公述作止於《六韜》，勛業形於一代，豈宜擬諸盛德，均其殊禮！

translations.literal: Moreover Lord Tai's writings extend only to the Six Secret Teachings, and his achievements were manifest in a single age—how can he be compared to supreme virtue and given equal extraordinary rites!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Lord Tai's writings extend only to the Six Secret Teachings, and his achievements were manifest in a single age—how can he be compared to supreme virtue and given equal extraordinary rites!

sentences.zh: 其祝文請不進署，『敢昭告』請改為『敬祭於』，『其昭告』請改為『致祭於留侯』，其獻官請準舊式，差太常卿已下充。」

translations.literal: As for the prayer text, please do not have it submitted for imperial signature; 'I dare proclaim' please be changed to 'I respectfully sacrifice to'; 'proclaim to him' please be changed to 'offer sacrifice to Marquis Liu'; as for the offering officials, please follow the old form and assign the Minister of Rites and those below."
translations.idiomatic: The prayer text should not be submitted for imperial signature; 'I dare proclaim' should be changed to 'I respectfully sacrifice to,' and 'proclaim to him' to 'offer sacrifice to Marquis Liu.' The offering officials should follow the old form, with the Minister of Rites and his subordinates assigned."

sentences.zh: 詔百僚進議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to submit opinions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all officials to submit opinions.

sentences.zh: 文武官上言，互有異同。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials memorialized, each with differing views.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials memorialized with differing views.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「帝德廣運，乃武乃文，文化武功，皇王之二柄，祀禮教敬，國章孔明。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The emperor's virtue extends far; he is both martial and civil. Civil transformation and martial achievement are the two handles of emperors and kings; sacrificial rites teach reverence—the nation's regulations are brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The emperor's virtue extends far; he is both martial and civil. Civil transformation and martial achievement are the two handles of kingship; sacrificial rites teach reverence—the nation's regulations are brilliantly clear.

sentences.zh: 自今宜上將軍以下充獻官，余依紓所奏。」

translations.literal: From now on the General-in-Chief and those below should serve as offering officials; the rest shall follow Shu's memorial."
translations.idiomatic: From now on the General-in-Chief and those below shall serve as offering officials; the rest shall follow Li Shu's memorial.

sentences.zh: 紓又奏詔為《興元紀功述》及郊廟樂章，諸所論著甚眾。

translations.literal: Shu also received edicts to compose the Account of Achievements at Xingyuan and suburban and temple music pieces; his various writings were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu also received edicts to compose the Account of Achievements at Xingyuan and suburban and temple music pieces; his writings were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年六十二。

translations.literal: He died in office at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan he was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan he was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 邵說邵說，相州安陽人。

translations.literal: Shao Yue—Shao Yue was a native of Anyang in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yue was a native of Anyang in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為史思明判官，歷事思明、朝義，常掌兵事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as administrative aide to Shi Siming; he successively served Siming and Chaoyi and often managed military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as administrative aide to Shi Siming, then continued under Siming and his son Chaoyi, often managing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝義之敗，說降於軍前，郭子儀愛其才，留於幕下。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi was defeated, Yue surrendered before the army; Guo Ziyi admired his talent and kept him on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyi was defeated, Shao Yue surrendered before the army; Guo Ziyi admired his talent and kept him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 累授長安令、秘書少監，遷吏部侍郎、太子詹事，以才幹稱。

translations.literal: He was successively appointed magistrate of Chang'an and vice director of the Secretariat, promoted to vice minister of Personnel and tutor to the heir apparent, and was known for talent and capability.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to magistrate of Chang'an and vice director of the Secretariat, then to vice minister of Personnel and tutor to the heir apparent, earning a reputation for talent and capability.

sentences.zh: 談者或以宰相許之，金吾將軍裴儆謂諫議大夫柳載曰：「以鄙夫所度，說得禍不久矣。

translations.literal: Some in conversation even promised him the chancellorship. Jinwu general Pei Jing said to remonstrating grand master Liu Zai, "By this humble man's estimate, Yue will meet disaster before long.
translations.idiomatic: Some even spoke of him as a future chancellor. Jinwu general Pei Jing told remonstrating grand master Liu Zai, "By my estimate, Shao Yue will meet disaster before long.

sentences.zh: 且說與史思明父子定君臣之分，居劇官，掌兵柄，亡軀犯順，前後百戰，於賊庭掠名家子女以為婢仆者數十人，剽盜寶貨，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Moreover Yue established the relation of ruler and minister with Shi Siming and his son, held weighty offices, wielded military power, risked his life in rebellion, fought in a hundred battles before and after, seized dozens of sons and daughters of eminent families in the rebel court to serve as maids and servants, and plundered treasures beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yue established the relation of ruler and minister with Shi Siming and his son, held weighty offices, wielded military power, and fought in a hundred battles in rebellion; in the rebel court he seized dozens of children of eminent families as servants and plundered treasures beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 力屈然後降，朝廷宥以不死。

translations.literal: Only when his strength was exhausted did he surrender; the court spared him from death.
translations.idiomatic: Only when his strength was exhausted did he surrender; the court spared his life.

sentences.zh: 獲齒班序，無厚顏，而又遑遑求財，崇飾第宅，附托貴幸，以求大用，不知愧懼，而有得色，其能久乎！」

translations.literal: He was allowed a place in the ranks without shame, yet again hurried to seek wealth, lavishly adorned his residence, relied on powerful favorites to seek great employment, knew neither shame nor fear, and wore a look of satisfaction—how can he last long!"
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed a place at court without shame, yet hurried to amass wealth, lavishly adorned his residence, and relied on powerful favorites to seek high office, showing neither shame nor fear but satisfaction—how can he last!

sentences.zh: 建中三年，嚴郢得罪，說與郢厚善，勸硃泚抗疏申其冤，說為草其奏，上知之，貶說歸州刺史，竟卒於貶所。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong Yan Yi offended; Yue was on close terms with Yi and urged Zhu Ci to submit a forthright memorial asserting his innocence; Yue drafted the memorial for him. When the emperor learned of it, Yue was demoted to prefect of Guizhou and ultimately died in his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong Yan Yi fell from favor; Shao Yue, who was close to him, urged Zhu Ci to submit a forthright memorial asserting his innocence and drafted it himself. When the emperor learned of this, Shao Yue was demoted to prefect of Guizhou and ultimately died in exile.

sentences.zh: 于邵于邵，字相門，其先家於代，今為京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Yu Shao—Yu Shao, courtesy name Xiangmen, his ancestors had their home in Dai and are now natives of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shao, whose courtesy name was Xiangmen, came from a family originally of Dai and was now registered as a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖筠，戶部尚書。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jun was Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu Jun served as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 邵天寶末進士登科，書判超絕，授崇文館校書郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era Shao passed the jinshi examination; his documentary judgments were outstanding, and he was appointed collator in the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era Yu Shao passed the jinshi examination; his documentary judgments were outstanding, and he was appointed collator in the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 累歷使府，入為起居郎，再遷比部郎中，尚二十考第於吏部，以當稱。

translations.literal: He successively served in commissioners' offices, entered the court as attendant of the emperor, was twice promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue, and still had twenty annual evaluations pending at the Ministry of Personnel—he was considered fitting for the post.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively in commissioners' offices, entered the court as attendant of the emperor, and was twice promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue while still having twenty annual evaluations pending at the Ministry of Personnel—he was considered well qualified.

sentences.zh: 無何，出為道州刺史，未就道，轉巴州。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as prefect of Daozhou; before he took up the post he was transferred to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent out as prefect of Daozhou but was transferred to Bazhou before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 時歲儉，夷獠數千相聚山澤，圍州掠眾，邵勵州兵以拒之。

translations.literal: At that time the year was lean; several thousand Yi and Liao gathered in mountains and marshes, besieged the prefecture, and plundered the people. Shao encouraged the prefectural troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: That year harvests were poor; several thousand tribal forces gathered in the hills, besieged the prefecture, and plundered the people. Yu Shao rallied the prefectural troops to resist them.

sentences.zh: 旬有二日，遣使說喻，盜邀邵面降，邵儒服出城，盜羅拜而降，圍解，節度使李抱玉以聞，超遷梓州，以疾不至，遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: After twelve days he sent envoys to persuade them; the bandits invited Shao to come in person to surrender. Shao put on scholar's robes and went out of the city; the bandits bowed in ranks and submitted, and the siege was lifted. Military commissioner Li Baoyu reported this, and Shao was promoted ahead of schedule to Zizhou; because of illness he did not go and was transferred to director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After twelve days he sent envoys to negotiate; the bandits invited Yu Shao to surrender in person. He went out in scholar's robes, and the bandits bowed in ranks and submitted, lifting the siege. Military commissioner Li Baoyu reported this, and Yu Shao was promoted ahead of schedule to Zizhou; illness kept him from going, and he was made director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使崔寧請留為支度副使。

translations.literal: Xichuan military commissioner Cui Ning requested that he be retained as deputy commissioner for fiscal support.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan military commissioner Cui Ning asked that he be retained as deputy commissioner for fiscal support.

sentences.zh: 尋拜諫議大夫、知制誥，再遷禮部侍郎、史館修撰，為三司使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed remonstrating grand master and put in charge of edicts, then twice promoted to vice minister of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute, and served as a three-commissioners envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed remonstrating grand master in charge of edicts, then twice promoted to vice minister of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute, and served as a three-commissioners envoy.

sentences.zh: 以撰上尊號冊，賜階三品，當時大詔令，皆出於邵。

translations.literal: For composing the book of the exalted honorific title he was granted third rank, and at that time major edicts all issued from Shao.
translations.idiomatic: For composing the book of the exalted honorific title he was granted third rank, and at that time major edicts all came from Yu Shao's pen.

sentences.zh: 頃之，與御史中丞袁高、給事中蔣鎮雜理左丞薛邕詔獄。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he joined chief censor Yuan Gao and supervising secretary Jiang Zhen in jointly handling the edict-case of Left Vice Director Xue Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he joined chief censor Yuan Gao and supervising secretary Jiang Zhen in jointly handling the edict-case of Left Vice Director Xue Yong.

sentences.zh: 邵以為邕犯在赦前，奏出之，失旨，貶桂州長史。

translations.literal: Shao held that Yong's offense fell before an amnesty and memorialized to release him; this missed the emperor's intent, and Shao was demoted to chief administrator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shao held that Xue Yong's offense fell before an amnesty and memorialized for his release; this displeased the emperor, and Yu Shao was demoted to chief administrator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，除原王傅，後為太子賓客，與宰相陸贄不睦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was appointed tutor to the Prince of Yuan, later became guest of the heir apparent, and was on bad terms with chief minister Lu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was appointed tutor to the Prince of Yuan, later became guest of the heir apparent, and was on bad terms with chief minister Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為杭州刺史，以疾請告，坐貶衢州別駕，移江州別駕，卒年八十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out as prefect of Hangzhou; he requested leave because of illness and was punished by demotion to vice-prefect of Quzhou, transferred to vice-prefect of Jiangzhou, and died at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was sent out as prefect of Hangzhou; he requested sick leave and was demoted to vice-prefect of Quzhou, then transferred to vice-prefect of Jiangzhou, where he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 邵性孝悌，內行修潔，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Shao was filial and brotherly by nature, refined and pure in private conduct, and became all the more earnest in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shao was filial and brotherly by nature, refined and pure in private conduct, and became all the more earnest in old age.

sentences.zh: 初，樊澤常舉賢良方正，邵一見之於京師，曰：「將相之材也。」

translations.literal: Earlier Fan Ze had often been recommended as worthy and upright; Shao saw him once in the capital and said, "This is material for generals and chancellors."
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Ze was recommended as worthy and upright, Yu Shao saw him once in the capital and said, "This is material for generals and chancellors.

sentences.zh: 不十五年，澤為節將。

translations.literal: Within fifteen years Ze became a military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Within fifteen years Fan Ze became a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 崔元翰年近五十，始舉進士，邵異其文，擢第甲科，且曰：「不十五年，當掌詔令。」

translations.literal: Cui Yuanhan was nearly fifty when he first passed the jinshi examination; Shao was struck by his writing, placed him in the top grade, and said, "Within fifteen years he will preside over edicts."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan was nearly fifty when he first passed the jinshi examination; Yu Shao was struck by his writing, placed him in the top grade, and said, "Within fifteen years he will preside over edicts.

sentences.zh: 竟如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it proved true.

sentences.zh: 獨孤授舉博學宏詞，吏部考為乙第，在中書覆升甲科，人稱其當。

translations.literal: Dugu Shou passed the erudite and literary examination; the Ministry of Personnel graded him in the second class, but the Secretariat on review raised him to the top class, and people said the judgment was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Shou passed the erudite and literary examination; the Ministry of Personnel graded him in the second class, but the Secretariat on review raised him to the top class, and people said the judgment was fitting.

sentences.zh: 有集四十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in forty juan.

sentences.zh: 崔元翰崔元翰者，博陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanhan—Cui Yuanhan was a native of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan was a native of Boling.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第，登博學宏詞制科，又應賢良方正、直言極諫科，三舉皆升甲第，年已五十余。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, passed the erudite and literary decree examination, and also responded to the worthy and upright and forthright remonstrance examinations—all three times rising to the top grade when he was already over fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, the erudite and literary decree examination, and the worthy and upright and forthright remonstrance examinations—all three times earning the top grade when he was already over fifty.

sentences.zh: 李汧公鎮滑臺，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Fen garrisoned Huatai, he recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Fen garrisoned Huatai, he recruited Cui Yuanhan as an aide.

sentences.zh: 後北平王馬燧在太原，聞其名，致禮命之，又為燧府掌書記。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Beiping Ma Sui was at Taiyuan, he heard his name, sent gifts and summoned him, and again had him serve as recorder on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Prince of Beiping Ma Sui was at Taiyuan, he heard of him, sent gifts and summoned him, and had him serve as recorder on his staff.

sentences.zh: 入朝為太常博士、禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered court service as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 竇參輔政，用為知制誥，詔令溫雅，合於典謨。

translations.literal: When Dou Can assisted in government, he was used as drafter of edicts; his edicts were warm and elegant and accorded with the canon of governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can assisted in government, Cui Yuanhan was made drafter of edicts; his edicts were warm and elegant and accorded with the canon of governance.

sentences.zh: 然性太剛褊簡傲，不能取容於時，每發言論，略無阿徇，忤執政旨，故掌誥二年，而官不遷。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was overly rigid, narrow, simple, and proud, unable to win accommodation in his time; whenever he expressed opinions he scarcely flattered or followed others, offended the intent of those in power, and therefore though he handled edicts for two years his office was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was overly rigid, narrow, and proud, unable to win accommodation at court; whenever he spoke he scarcely flattered those in power, and though he handled edicts for two years his office was not promoted.

sentences.zh: 竟罷知制誥，守比部郎中。

translations.literal: In the end he was removed from drafting edicts and kept his post as director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was removed from drafting edicts and retained only his post as director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元翰苦心文章，時年七十余，好學不倦。

translations.literal: Yuanhan labored at his writing; at the time he was over seventy and loved learning without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan labored at his writing; even past seventy he loved learning without tiring.

sentences.zh: 既介獨耿直，故少交遊，唯秉一操，伏膺翰墨。

translations.literal: Being upright, solitary, and direct, he had few social ties and held to a single principle, devoting himself to brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, solitary, and direct, he had few social ties and held to a single principle, devoting himself to literature.

sentences.zh: 其對策及奏記、碑誌、師法班固、蔡伯喈，而致思精密。

translations.literal: His policy essays, memorials, stele inscriptions, and epitaphs took Ban Gu and Cai Yong as models, and his thought was refined and precise.
translations.idiomatic: His policy essays, memorials, stele inscriptions, and epitaphs took Ban Gu and Cai Yong as models, with refined and precise thought.

sentences.zh: 為時所擯，終於散位。

translations.literal: He was rejected by his age and ended in an unsalaried post.
translations.idiomatic: Rejected by his age, he ended his career in an unsalaried post.

sentences.zh: 于公異于公異者，吳人。

translations.literal: Yu Gongyi—Yu Gongyi was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gongyi was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，文章精拔，為時所稱。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; his essays were refined and outstanding and were praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination; his writing was refined and outstanding and won praise from his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 建中末，為李晟招討府掌書記。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong he served as recorder on Li Sheng's pacification headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jianzhong he served as recorder on Li Sheng's pacification headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，收京城，公異為露布上行在云：「臣已肅清宮禁，祗奏寢園，鐘虡不移，廟貌如故。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, when the capital was recovered, Gongyi's victory bulletin to the mobile court read, "Your servant has already cleared the palace precincts and respectfully reports on the imperial tombs; bells and stands have not been moved, and the temple appearance is as before."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan, when the capital was recovered, Yu Gongyi's victory bulletin to the mobile court read, "Your servant has already cleared the palace precincts and respectfully reports on the imperial tombs; bells and stands have not been moved, and the temple appearance is as before.

sentences.zh: 德宗覽之，泣下不自勝，左右為之嗚咽。

translations.literal: When Dezong read it, tears flowed beyond his control, and those at his side sobbed for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong read it, tears flowed beyond his control, and those at his side sobbed with him.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「不知誰為之？」

translations.literal: Then he said, "I do not know who wrote this?"
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "I do not know who wrote this?

sentences.zh: 或對曰：「于公異之詞也。」

translations.literal: Someone replied, "It is the wording of Yu Gongyi."
translations.idiomatic: Someone replied, "It is the wording of Yu Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 上稱善久之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it at length.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it at length.

sentences.zh: 公異初應進士時，與舉人陸贄不協；

translations.literal: When Gongyi first responded to the jinshi examination, he was not on good terms with candidate Lu Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Gongyi first took the jinshi examination, he was not on good terms with fellow candidate Lu Zhi;

sentences.zh: 至是贄為翰林學士，聞上稱與，尤不悅。

translations.literal: by this time Zhi was a Hanlin academician; when he heard the emperor's praise, he was especially displeased.
translations.idiomatic: by this time Lu Zhi was a Hanlin academician; when he heard the emperor's praise, he was especially displeased.

sentences.zh: 時議者言之，公異少時不為後母所容，自遊宦成名，不歸鄉里；

translations.literal: At that time those in public discussion spoke of it: in his youth Gongyi was not accepted by his stepmother; once he achieved fame through official service, he did not return to his home district;
translations.idiomatic: At that time critics noted that in his youth Yu Gongyi had not been accepted by his stepmother and that once he achieved fame through office he never returned home;

sentences.zh: 及貞元中陸贄為宰相，奏公異無素行，黜之。

translations.literal: when in the Zhenyuan era Lu Zhi became chief minister, he memorialized that Gongyi lacked proper conduct and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: when in the Zhenyuan era Lu Zhi became chief minister, he memorialized that Yu Gongyi lacked proper conduct and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「祠部員外郎于公異，頃以才名，升於省闥。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Vice director in the Ministry of Rites Yu Gongyi was recently raised to the inner offices on account of literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Vice director in the Ministry of Rites Yu Gongyi was recently raised to the inner offices on account of literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 其少也，為父母之所不容，宜其引慝在躬，孝行不匱，匿名跡於畎畝，候安否於門閭，俾其親之過不彰，庶其誠之至必感。

translations.literal: In his youth he was not accepted by his parents; he ought to have kept guilt upon himself and never ceased in filial conduct, concealed his tracks in the fields, and watched for their well-being at the gate and lane, so that his parents' faults would not be exposed and his utmost sincerity might surely move them.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was not accepted by his parents; he ought to have borne guilt upon himself and never ceased in filial conduct, concealed his tracks in the fields, and watched for their well-being at the gate and lane, so that his parents' faults would not be exposed and his utmost sincerity might move them.

sentences.zh: 安於棄斥，遊學遠方，忘其溫凊之戀，竟至存亡之隔，為人子者，忍至是乎！

translations.literal: Content with rejection, he studied and traveled far away, forgot his longing for their warmth and cool, and came even to the separation of life and death—for a son to be so hard-hearted!
translations.idiomatic: Content with rejection, he studied and traveled far away, forgot his longing for their comfort, and came even to the separation of life and death—for a son to be so hard-hearted!

sentences.zh: 宜放歸田里，俾自循省。

translations.literal: He should be sent back to the fields and villages to examine himself.
translations.idiomatic: He should be sent back to the countryside to examine himself.

sentences.zh: 其舉公異官尚書左丞盧邁，宜奪俸兩月。」

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Lu Mai, who recommended Gongyi for office, should have two months' salary withheld."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Lu Mai, who recommended Yu Gongyi for office, should have two months' salary withheld.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人高郢薦監察御史元敦義，及睹公異譴逐，懼為所累，乃上疏首陳敦義虧於禮教，詔嘉郢之知過，俾敦義罷歸。

translations.literal: At that time drafting secretary Gao Ying had recommended investigating censor Yuan Dunyi; on seeing Gongyi's dismissal and fearing to be implicated, he submitted a memorial first declaring that Dunyi was deficient in ritual teaching. An edict praised Ying's knowledge of his fault and had Dunyi dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: At that time drafting secretary Gao Ying had recommended investigating censor Yuan Dunyi; on seeing Yu Gongyi's dismissal and fearing implication, he submitted a memorial first declaring that Dunyi was deficient in ritual teaching. An edict praised Gao Ying's awareness of his error and had Dunyi dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 公異竟名位不振，感軻而卒，人士惜其才，惡贄之褊急焉。

translations.literal: Gongyi in the end never achieved fame or position, died of grief, and men of letters regretted his talent and hated Zhi's narrow hastiness.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gongyi never achieved fame or high office, died of grief, and men of letters regretted his talent while condemning Lu Zhi's narrow hastiness.

sentences.zh: 呂渭呂渭，字君載，河中人。

translations.literal: Lü Wei—Lü Wei, courtesy name Junzai, was a native of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wei, whose courtesy name was Junzai, was a native of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 父延之，越州刺史、浙江東道節度使。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi was prefect of Yuezhou and military commissioner of Zhedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lü Yanzhi served as prefect of Yuezhou and military commissioner of Zhedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 渭舉進士，累授婺州永康令、大理評事。

translations.literal: Wei passed the jinshi examination and was successively appointed magistrate of Yongkang in Wuzhou and reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wei passed the jinshi examination and was successively appointed magistrate of Yongkang in Wuzhou and reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李涵辟為支使，再遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Zhexi observation commissioner Li Han recruited him as an administrative aide, and after two promotions he became attendant censor in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhexi observation commissioner Li Han recruited him as an administrative aide, and after two promotions he became attendant censor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 涵自御史大夫改太子少傅，渭上言：「涵父名少康，今涵為少傅，恐乖朝典。」

translations.literal: When Han was changed from chief censor to Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, Wei memorialized, "Han's father's name was Shaokang; now Han is Junior Tutor—I fear this violates court regulations."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Han was changed from chief censor to Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, Lü Wei memorialized, "Li Han's father's name was Shaokang; now Li Han is Junior Tutor—I fear this violates court regulations.

sentences.zh: 由是特授渭司門員外郎。

translations.literal: For this Wei was specially appointed vice director in the Ministry of Justice for the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: For this Lü Wei was specially appointed vice director in the Ministry of Justice for the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 尋為御史臺劾奏：「涵再任少卿，此時都不言；

translations.literal: Soon the Censorate impeached and memorialized, "When Han twice held the post of vice minister, at that time Wei said nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Censorate impeached him, saying, "When Li Han twice held the post of vice minister, Lü Wei said nothing at the time;

sentences.zh: 今為少傅，疑以散慢，乃為不可。」

translations.literal: now that he is Junior Tutor, it is suspected that out of laxity he declared it impossible."
translations.idiomatic: now that Li Han is Junior Tutor, it is suspected that out of laxity he declared it improper.

sentences.zh: 由是貶渭歙州司馬，改涵檢校工部尚書、兼光祿卿。

translations.literal: For this Wei was demoted to vice prefect of Shezhou, and Han was changed to acting Minister of Works with concurrent rank as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: For this Lü Wei was demoted to vice prefect of Shezhou, and Li Han was changed to acting Minister of Works with concurrent rank as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 渭累授舒州刺史、吏部員外、駕部郎中、知制詔、中書舍人，母憂罷。

translations.literal: Wei was successively appointed prefect of Shuzhou, vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, director in the Ministry of War for the Chariot Office, drafter of edicts, and drafting secretary, then left office for mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wei was successively appointed prefect of Shuzhou, vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, director in the Ministry of War for the Chariot Office, drafter of edicts, and drafting secretary, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授太子右庶子、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he was appointed Right Vice Director in the heir apparent's household and vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he was appointed Right Vice Director in the heir apparent's household and vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 中書省有柳樹，建中末枯死，興元元年車駕還京後，其樹再榮，人謂之瑞柳。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat there was a willow tree that withered and died at the end of Jianzhong; after the imperial carriage returned to the capital in the first year of Xingyuan the tree flourished again, and people called it the auspicious willow.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat there was a willow tree that withered and died at the end of Jianzhong; after the imperial carriage returned to the capital in the first year of Xingyuan the tree flourished again, and people called it the auspicious willow.

sentences.zh: 渭試進士，取瑞柳為賦題，上聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: When Wei tested jinshi candidates he took the auspicious willow as the fu topic; the emperor heard of it and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wei tested jinshi candidates he took the auspicious willow as the fu topic; the emperor heard of it and praised him.

sentences.zh: 渭又結附裴延齡之子操，舉進士，文詞非工，渭擢之登第，為正人嗤鄙。

translations.literal: Wei also attached himself to Pei Yanling's son Cao; when Cao took the jinshi examination his literary style was not skilled, yet Wei promoted him to pass, and upright men scorned him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wei also attached himself to Pei Yanling's son Cao; when Cao took the jinshi examination his writing was poor, yet Lü Wei promoted him to pass, and upright men scorned him for it.

sentences.zh: 因入閣遺失請托文記，遂出為潭州刺史、兼御史中丞、湖南都團練觀察使，在任三歲，政甚煩碎。

translations.literal: Because he lost a record of solicitation when entering the inner court, he was sent out as prefect of Tanzhou with concurrent rank as chief censor and military training and observation commissioner of Hunan; during three years in office his government was very trivial and minute.
translations.idiomatic: Because he lost a record of solicitation when entering the inner court, he was sent out as prefect of Tanzhou with concurrent rank as chief censor and military training and observation commissioner of Hunan; during three years in office his administration was very trivial and minute.

sentences.zh: 貞元十六年卒，年六十六，贈陜州大都督。

translations.literal: He died in the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan at age sixty-six and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Protector of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously honored as Grand Protector of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 子溫、恭、儉、讓。

translations.literal: His sons were Wen, Gong, Jian, and Rang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wen, Gong, Jian, and Rang.

sentences.zh: 子 溫溫，字化光，貞元末登進士第，與翰林學士韋執誼善。

translations.literal: His son Wen—Wen, courtesy name Huaguang, passed the jinshi examination at the end of Zhenyuan and was on good terms with Hanlin academician Wei Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lü Wen, whose courtesy name was Huaguang, passed the jinshi examination at the end of Zhenyuan and was on good terms with Hanlin academician Wei Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 順宗在東宮，侍書王叔文勸太子招納時之英俊以自輔，溫與執誼尤為叔文所睠，起家再命拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong was in the Eastern Palace, attendant scribe Wang Shuwen urged the heir apparent to recruit outstanding men of the time to assist him; Wen and Zhiyi were especially favored by Shuwen, and from their first appointments were twice named Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong was crown prince, attendant scribe Wang Shuwen urged him to recruit outstanding men of the time; Lü Wen and Wei Zhiyi were especially favored by Shuwen and from their first appointments were twice named Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 二十年冬，副工部侍郎張薦為入吐蕃使，行至鳳翔，轉侍御史，賜緋袍牙笏。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twentieth year he served as deputy to Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jian on a mission to Tibet; when they reached Fengxiang he was transferred to attendant censor and granted a crimson robe and ivory tablet.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twentieth year he served as deputy to Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jian on a mission to Tibet; when they reached Fengxiang he was transferred to attendant censor and granted a crimson robe and ivory tablet.

sentences.zh: 明年，德宗晏駕，順宗即位，張薦卒於青海，吐蕃以中國喪禍，留溫經年。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Dezong passed away and Shunzong took the throne; Zhang Jian died at Qinghai, and Tibet, citing China's mourning calamity, detained Wen for a year.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Emperor Dezong died and Emperor Shunzong acceded; Zhang Jian died at Qinghai, and Tibet, citing China's mourning, detained Lü Wen for a year.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文用事，故與溫同遊東宮者，皆不次任用，溫在蕃中，悲嘆久之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shuwen was in power; those who had associated with Wen in the Eastern Palace were all appointed out of turn, while Wen was in Tibet and lamented for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Shuwen was in power; those who had associated with Lü Wen in the Eastern Palace were all appointed out of turn, while Lü Wen was in Tibet and lamented for a long time.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，使還，轉戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he returned from the mission and was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe he returned from the mission and was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時柳宗元等九人坐叔文貶逐。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Zongyuan and nine others were punished because of Shuwen and banished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Zongyuan and nine others were punished because of Shuwen and banished.

sentences.zh: 唯溫以奉使免。

translations.literal: Only Wen was spared because of his mission.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lü Wen was spared because of his mission.

sentences.zh: 溫天才俊拔，文彩贍逸，為時流柳宗元、劉禹錫所稱。

translations.literal: Wen had outstanding natural talent; his literary coloring was rich and flowing, and he was praised by contemporaries Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wen had outstanding natural talent; his writing was rich and flowing, and he was praised by contemporaries Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi.

sentences.zh: 然性多險詐，好奇近利，與竇群、羊士諤趣尚相狎。
