translations.literal: Yet by nature he was much given to treachery and deceit, curious about novelty and drawn to profit, and was intimate in tastes with Dou Qun and Yang Shie.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was much given to treachery and deceit, curious about novelty and drawn to profit, and was intimate in tastes with Dou Qun and Yang Shie.

sentences.zh: 群為韋夏卿所薦，自處士不數年至御史中丞，李吉甫尤奇待之。

translations.literal: Qun was recommended by Wei Xiaqing; from recluse scholar in a few years he reached chief censor, and Li Jiji especially regarded him with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Qun was recommended by Wei Xiaqing; from recluse scholar he rose within a few years to chief censor, and Li Jiji especially regarded him with wonder.

sentences.zh: 三年，吉甫為中官所惡，將出鎮揚州，溫欲乘其有間傾之。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiji was hated by palace eunuchs and was about to go out to garrison Yangzhou; Wen wished to seize an opening to overthrow him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Li Jiji was hated by palace eunuchs and was about to go out to garrison Yangzhou; Lü Wen wished to seize an opening to overthrow him.

sentences.zh: 溫自司封員外郎轉刑部郎中，竇群請為知雜。

translations.literal: Wen was transferred from vice director in the Ministry of Rites for the Seals Office to director in the Ministry of Justice; Dou Qun requested to serve as chief of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wen was transferred from vice director in the Ministry of Rites for the Seals Office to director in the Ministry of Justice; Dou Qun requested to serve as chief of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 吉甫以疾在第，召醫人陳登診視，夜宿於安邑裏第。

translations.literal: Jiji was ill at his residence and summoned the physician Chen Deng to examine him; Deng lodged overnight at the residence in Anyi Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiji was ill at his residence and summoned the physician Chen Deng to examine him; Deng lodged overnight at the residence in Anyi Lane.

sentences.zh: 溫伺知之，詰旦，令吏捕登鞫問之，又奏劾吉甫交通術士。

translations.literal: Wen learned of this by spying; at dawn he ordered clerks to seize Deng and interrogate him, and also memorialized to impeach Jiji for associating with occultists.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wen learned of this by spying; at dawn he ordered clerks to seize Chen Deng and interrogate him, and also memorialized to impeach Li Jiji for associating with occultists.

sentences.zh: 憲宗異之，召登面訊，其事皆虛，乃貶群為湖南觀察使，羊士諤資州刺史，溫均州刺史。

translations.literal: Xianzong was surprised and summoned Deng for face-to-face questioning; the matter was entirely false, and Qun was demoted to observation commissioner of Hunan, Yang Shie to prefect of Zizhou, and Wen to prefect of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was surprised and summoned Chen Deng for questioning; the charges were entirely false, and Dou Qun was demoted to observation commissioner of Hunan, Yang Shie to prefect of Zizhou, and Lü Wen to prefect of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝議以所責太輕，群再貶黔南，溫貶道州刺史。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that the punishments were too light; Qun was again demoted to Qiannan, and Wen to prefect of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion held that the punishments were too light; Dou Qun was again demoted to Qiannan, and Lü Wen to prefect of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉衡州，秩滿歸京，不得意，發疾卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Hengzhou; when his term ended he returned to the capital, was discontented, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Hengzhou; when his term ended he returned to the capital, was discontented, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 溫文體富艷，有丘明、班固之風，所著《淩煙閣功臣銘》、《張始興畫贊》、《移博士書》，頗為文士所賞，有文集十卷。

translations.literal: Wen's literary style was rich and ornate, with the manner of Qiu Ming and Ban Gu; his works the Inscription on Meritorious Ministers at Lingyan Pavilion, Eulogy on Zhang Shixing's Painting, and Letter Transferring the Erudite were much admired by men of letters, and he had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wen's literary style was rich and ornate, in the manner of Zuo Qiuming and Ban Gu; his works the Inscription on Meritorious Ministers at Lingyan Pavilion, Eulogy on Zhang Shixing's Painting, and Letter Transferring the Erudite were much admired by men of letters, and he left a collected works in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子 恭、儉恭、儉皆至侍御史，讓至太子右庶子，皆有美才。

translations.literal: His sons Gong and Jian—Gong and Jian both reached attendant censor, and Rang reached Right Vice Director in the heir apparent's household; all had fine talent.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Gong and Jian both reached attendant censor, and Rang reached Right Vice Director in the heir apparent's household; all had fine talent.

sentences.zh: 自後吉甫再入中書，長慶以後，李德裕黨盛，呂氏諸子無至達官者。

translations.literal: Afterward Jiji again entered the Secretariat; after Changqing, Li Deyu's faction flourished, and none of the Lü sons reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Li Jiji again entered the Secretariat; after Changqing, Li Deyu's faction flourished, and none of the Lü sons reached high office.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲逵鄭雲逵，滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yunkui—Zheng Yunkui was a native of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunkui was a native of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，舉進士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dali era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 性果誕敢言。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold, unrestrained, and daring in speech.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold, unrestrained, and daring in speech.

sentences.zh: 客遊兩河，以畫幹於硃泚，泚悅，乃表為節度掌書記、檢校祠部員外郎，仍以弟滔女妻之。

translations.literal: Traveling as a guest in the two He regions, he presented his painting to Zhu Ci; Ci was pleased and memorialized that he serve as military commission recorder and acting vice director in the Ministry of Rites for the Sacrificial Office, and also gave him his younger brother Tao's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling as a guest in the two He regions, he presented his painting to Zhu Ci; Ci was pleased and had him serve as military commission recorder and acting vice director in the Ministry of Rites for the Sacrificial Office, and also gave him his younger brother Zhu Tao's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 泚將入覲，先令雲逵入奏；

translations.literal: When Ci was about to enter court audience, he first had Yunkui go in to memorialize;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci was about to enter court audience, he first had Zheng Yunkui go in to memorialize;

sentences.zh: 及泚至京，以事怒雲逵，奏貶莫州參軍。

translations.literal: when Ci reached the capital he was angry with Yunkui over a matter and memorialized to demote him to aide in Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhu Ci reached the capital he was angry with Zheng Yunkui over a matter and memorialized to demote him to aide in Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 滔代泚後，請為判官。

translations.literal: After Tao replaced Ci, he requested Yunkui as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Tao replaced Zhu Ci, he requested Zheng Yunkui as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 滔助田悅為逆，雲逵渝之不從，遂棄妻子馳歸長安，帝嘉其來，留於客省，超拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Tao aided Tian Yue in rebellion, Yunkui admonished him but he would not follow; Yunkui then abandoned wife and children and galloped back to Chang'an. The emperor praised his coming, kept him in the guest bureau, and promoted him ahead of schedule to remonstrating grand master.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao aided Tian Yue in rebellion, Zheng Yunkui admonished him but he would not listen; Yunkui then abandoned wife and children and galloped back to Chang'an. The emperor praised his return, kept him in the guest bureau, and promoted him ahead of schedule to remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 奉天之難，雲逵奔赴行在，李晟以為行軍司馬，戎略多以咨之。

translations.literal: During the crisis at Fengtian, Yunkui rushed to the mobile court; Li Sheng made him march army marshal, and often consulted him on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis at Fengtian, Zheng Yunkui rushed to the mobile court; Li Sheng made him march army marshal and often consulted him on military strategy.

sentences.zh: 歷秘書少監、給事中，尋拜大理卿，遷刑部、兵部二侍郎、遷御史中丞，充順宗山陵橋道置頓使。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice director of the Secretariat, supervising secretary, and soon was appointed chief of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to vice minister of Justice and vice minister of War, then chief censor, and served as commissioner for arranging halts on the bridge road to Emperor Shunzong's mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as vice director of the Secretariat and supervising secretary, soon became chief of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to vice minister of Justice and vice minister of War, then chief censor, and served as commissioner for arranging halts on the bridge road to Emperor Shunzong's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 雲逵初為硃泚判官，常忤同幕蔡庭玉；

translations.literal: When Yunkui first served as Zhu Ci's administrative aide, he often offended fellow staff member Cai Tingyu;
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yunkui first served as Zhu Ci's administrative aide, he often offended fellow staff member Cai Tingyu;

sentences.zh: 庭玉白泚，黜為莫州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Tingyu reported to Ci, and Yunkui was dismissed to recording secretary in Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu reported to Zhu Ci, and Zheng Yunkui was dismissed to recording secretary in Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 滔復奏為判官，因深構庭玉於滔；

translations.literal: Tao again memorialized for him as administrative aide, and Yunkui therefore deeply framed Tingyu before Tao;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao again had him serve as administrative aide, and Zheng Yunkui therefore deeply framed Cai Tingyu before Zhu Tao;

sentences.zh: 滔為泚留後事，有請於泚，庭玉又輒隳之。

translations.literal: when Tao handled affairs as Ci's acting commissioner, if there was a request to Ci, Tingyu would again promptly destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhu Tao handled affairs as Zhu Ci's acting commissioner, if there was a request to Zhu Ci, Cai Tingyu would again promptly thwart it.

sentences.zh: 又有判官硃體微，亦蒙泚親信，與庭玉常從容言於泚曰：「滔非長者，不可付以兵權。」

translations.literal: There was also administrative aide Zhu Tiwai, who likewise enjoyed Ci's personal trust; with Tingyu he often spoke at ease to Ci, saying, "Tao is not a man of mature character and cannot be entrusted with military authority."
translations.idiomatic: There was also administrative aide Zhu Tiwai, who likewise enjoyed Zhu Ci's personal trust; with Cai Tingyu he often spoke at ease to Zhu Ci, saying, "Zhu Tao is not a man of mature character and cannot be entrusted with military authority.

sentences.zh: 滔竊知之。

translations.literal: Tao secretly learned of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao secretly learned of this.

sentences.zh: 後滔南討有功，雲逵數激怒之，滔乃抗表論庭玉等離間骨肉；

translations.literal: Later when Tao had merit in the southern campaign, Yunkui repeatedly provoked him, and Tao therefore submitted a forthright memorial accusing Tingyu and others of sowing discord between flesh and blood;
translations.idiomatic: Later when Zhu Tao had merit in the southern campaign, Zheng Yunkui repeatedly provoked him, and Zhu Tao therefore submitted a forthright memorial accusing Cai Tingyu and others of sowing discord between brothers;

sentences.zh: 及滔叛，帝乃召泚以表示之，故歸罪於庭玉等以悅滔，滔亦終叛。

translations.literal: when Tao rebelled the emperor summoned Ci and showed him the memorial, and therefore placed blame on Tingyu and others to please Tao—but Tao rebelled in the end anyway.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhu Tao rebelled the emperor summoned Zhu Ci and showed him the memorial, and therefore placed blame on Cai Tingyu and others to please Zhu Tao—but Zhu Tao rebelled in the end anyway.

sentences.zh: 三年，雲逵奏：其弟前太仆丞方逵，「受性兇悖，不知君親，眾惡備身，訓教莫及，結聚兇黨，江中劫人。

translations.literal: In the third year Yunkui memorialized concerning his younger brother, former vice director in the Court of the Imperial Stud Fangkui, "By nature he is fierce and perverse, knows neither ruler nor parent, is hated by all, and teaching cannot reach him; he gathers violent factions and robs people on the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zheng Yunkui memorialized concerning his younger brother, former vice director in the Court of the Imperial Stud Fangkui, "By nature he is fierce and perverse, knows neither ruler nor parent, is hated by all, and teaching cannot reach him; he gathers violent factions and robs people on the river.

sentences.zh: 臣亡父先臣昈杖至一百，終不能斃。

translations.literal: Your servant's deceased father, the late minister Huan, beat him up to a hundred strokes and still could not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's deceased father, the late minister Huan, beat him up to a hundred strokes and still could not kill him.

sentences.zh: 張延賞任揚州日，亦曾犯延賞法，決殺復蘇。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yanshang was in Yangzhou he also once violated Yanshang's law and was sentenced to death but revived.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yanshang was in Yangzhou he also once violated Yanshang's law and was sentenced to death but revived.

sentences.zh: 至於常言，皆呼臣亡父先臣名，親戚所知，無可教語。

translations.literal: As for his usual speech, he always calls out the personal names of your servant's deceased father and late minister; relatives know this—there is nothing by which he can be taught.
translations.idiomatic: As for his usual speech, he always calls out the personal names of your servant's deceased father and late minister; relatives know this—there is nothing by which he can be taught.

sentences.zh: 昨聞於邠、寧、慶等州幹謁節度及州縣乞丐，今見在武功縣南，西戎俯近，恐有異謀；

translations.literal: Yesterday I heard that in Bin, Ning, Qing, and other prefectures he importunes military commissioners and prefectural and county officials as a beggar; he is now seen south of Wugong county, with Western Rong close at hand—I fear he has sinister designs;
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I heard that in Bin, Ning, Qing, and other prefectures he importunes military commissioners and local officials as a beggar; he is now seen south of Wugong county, with Western Rong close at hand—I fear he has sinister designs;

sentences.zh: 若不冒死奏聞，必恐覆臣家族。」

translations.literal: if I do not risk death to report this, I fear he will destroy your servant's entire clan."
translations.idiomatic: if I do not risk death to report this, I fear he will destroy your servant's entire clan.

sentences.zh: 詔令京兆府錮身遞送黔州，付李模於僻遠州驅使，勿許東西。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Jingzhao prefecture to shackle him and escort him by relay to Qianzhou, hand him to Li Mo to be driven in a remote prefecture, and not permit him to go east or west.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Jingzhao prefecture to shackle him and escort him by relay to Qianzhou, hand him to Li Mo to be driven in a remote prefecture, and not permit him to go east or west.

sentences.zh: 雲逵元和元年拜右金吾衛大將軍，歲中改京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe Yunkui was appointed general of the Right Jinwu Guard; within the year he was changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe Zheng Yunkui was appointed general of the Right Jinwu Guard; within the year he was changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 五年五月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth month of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 李益李益，肅宗朝宰相揆之族子。

translations.literal: Li Yi—Li Yi was a clansman of chief minister Hui in the Suzong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was a clansman of chief minister Li Hui in the Suzong reign.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，長為歌詩。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and excelled at songs and poems.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and excelled at songs and poems.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，與宗人李賀齊名。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan he was equally famous with his clansman Li He.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenyuan he was equally famous with his clansman Li He.

sentences.zh: 每作一篇，為教坊樂人以賂求取。

translations.literal: Whenever he produced a piece, musicians of the Music Bureau would bribe to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he produced a new piece, musicians of the Music Bureau would bribe to obtain it.

sentences.zh: 唱為供奉歌詞。

translations.literal: They sang them as lyrics for imperial service.
translations.idiomatic: They sang them as lyrics for imperial service.

sentences.zh: 其《征人歌》、《早行篇》，好事者畫為屏障；

translations.literal: His Song of the Campaigner and Early Journey were painted as screens by enthusiasts;
translations.idiomatic: His Song of the Campaigner and Early Journey were painted as screens by enthusiasts;

sentences.zh: 「回樂峰前沙似雪，受降城外月如霜」之句，天下以為歌詞。

translations.literal: the lines "Before Huile Peak the sand is like snow; outside Shouxiang city the moon is like frost" were taken throughout the realm as song lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: the lines "Before Huile Peak the sand is like snow; outside Shouxiang city the moon is like frost" were taken throughout the realm as song lyrics.

sentences.zh: 然少有癡病，而多猜忌，防閑妻妾，過為苛酷，而有散灰扃戶之譚聞於時，故時謂妒癡為「李益疾」；

translations.literal: Yet he had a slight affliction of obsession and was much given to suspicion; his guarding of wife and concubines was excessively harsh, and there was talk at the time of scattering ash and bolting doors, so contemporaries called jealous obsession "Li Yi's ailment";
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had a slight affliction of obsession and was much given to suspicion; his guarding of wife and concubines was excessively harsh, and there was talk at the time of scattering ash and bolting doors, so contemporaries called jealous obsession "Li Yi's ailment";

sentences.zh: 以是久之不調，而流輩皆居顯位。

translations.literal: for this reason he long went without promotion while his contemporaries all held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: for this reason he long went without promotion while his contemporaries all held eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 益不得意，北遊河朔，幽州劉濟辟為從事，常與濟詩而有「不上望京樓」之句。

translations.literal: Yi was discontent, traveled north to Heshuo, and was recruited as an aide by Liu Ji of Youzhou; he often composed poems with Ji and had the line "not ascending Wangjing Tower."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was discontent, traveled north to Heshuo, and was recruited as an aide by Liu Ji of Youzhou; he often composed poems with Ji and had the line "not ascending Wangjing Tower."

sentences.zh: 憲宗雅聞其名，自河北召還，用為秘書少監、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: Xianzong had long heard his name and recalled him from Hebei, appointing him vice director of the Secretariat and academician of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong had long heard his name and recalled him from Hebei, appointing him vice director of the Secretariat and academician of the Jixian Hall.

sentences.zh: 自負才地，多所淩忽，為眾不容，諫官舉其幽州詩句，降居散秩。

translations.literal: Confident in his talent and standing, he often looked down on others and was not tolerated by the multitude; remonstrating officials cited his Youzhou poem lines, and he was demoted to an unsalaried rank.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his talent and standing, he often looked down on others and was not tolerated at court; remonstrating officials cited his Youzhou poem lines, and he was demoted to an unsalaried rank.

sentences.zh: 俄復用為秘書監，遷太子賓客、集賢學士判院事，轉右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was again used as director of the Secretariat, promoted to guest of the heir apparent and academician of the Jixian Hall presiding over institute affairs, and transferred to Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed director of the Secretariat, promoted to guest of the heir apparent and academician of the Jixian Hall presiding over institute affairs, and transferred to Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太和初，以禮部尚書致仕，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he retired as Minister of Rites and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe he retired as Minister of Rites and died.

sentences.zh: 李賀李賀，字長吉，宗室鄭王之後。

translations.literal: Li He—Li He, courtesy name Changji, was a descendant of the imperial house, the Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li He, whose courtesy name was Changji, was a descendant of the imperial house, the Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 父名晉肅，以是不應進士，韓愈為之作《諱辨》，賀竟不就試。

translations.literal: His father's name was Jinsu, and for this reason he did not respond to the jinshi examination; Han Yu wrote the Taboo Discourse for him, yet He in the end did not take the test.
translations.idiomatic: His father's name was Jinsu, and for this reason he did not take the jinshi examination; Han Yu wrote the Taboo Discourse for him, yet Li He in the end did not take the test.

sentences.zh: 手筆敏捷，尤長於歌篇。

translations.literal: His brush was nimble, and he especially excelled at songs.
translations.idiomatic: His brush was nimble, and he especially excelled at songs.

sentences.zh: 其文思體勢，如崇巖峭壁，萬仞崛起，當時文士從而效之，無能仿佛者。

translations.literal: The cast of his literary thought was like lofty cliffs and sheer precipices rising ten thousand ren; men of letters of the time followed and imitated him, but none could approximate him.
translations.idiomatic: The cast of his literary thought was like lofty cliffs and sheer precipices rising ten thousand ren; men of letters of the time followed and imitated him, but none could approximate him.

sentences.zh: 其樂府詞數十篇，至於雲韶樂工，無不諷誦。

translations.literal: His several dozen yuefu lyrics—even the Yunshao musicians all chanted and recited them.
translations.idiomatic: His several dozen yuefu lyrics—even the Yunshao musicians all chanted and recited them.

sentences.zh: 補太常寺協律郎，卒，時年二十四。

translations.literal: He was appointed harmonics officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died at age twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed harmonics officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died at the age of twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 贊史臣曰：文學之士，代不乏才。

translations.literal: The praising historian says: Men of letters have never lacked talent in any age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Men of letters have never lacked talent in any age.

sentences.zh: 永泰、貞元之間，如徐浩、趙涓諸公，可謂一時之秀也。

translations.literal: Between Yongtai and Zhenyuan, such men as Xu Hao and Zhao Juan may be called the outstanding talents of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yongtai and Zhenyuan, such men as Xu Hao and Zhao Juan may be called the outstanding talents of their time.

sentences.zh: 然太真以畏懦聞，邵說以僭侈失，于公異、呂渭、李益皆有微累，故知全其德者罕矣。

translations.literal: Yet Taizhen was known for timidity and cowardice, Shao Yue was lost through presumptuous extravagance, and Yu Gongyi, Lü Wei, and Li Yi all had slight stains—thus one knows that those who preserved their virtue whole were few.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Taizhen was known for timidity and cowardice, Shao Yue was lost through presumptuous extravagance, and Yu Gongyi, Lü Wei, and Li Yi all had slight stains—thus one knows that those who preserved their virtue whole were few.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：名以才顯，才兼德尊。

translations.literal: The praise says: Names are displayed through talent; talent joined with virtue is honored.
translations.idiomatic: The praise says: Names are displayed through talent; talent joined with virtue is honored.

sentences.zh: 徐、趙、劉、李，厥聲遠聞。

translations.literal: Xu, Zhao, Liu, and Li—their fame was heard from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, Zhao, Liu, and Li—their fame was heard from afar.

sentences.zh: 邵、于、呂、鄭，其名久存。

translations.literal: Shao, Yu, Lü, and Zheng—their names long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, Yu, Lü, and Zheng—their names long endure.

sentences.zh: 半乏全德，愧於後人。

translations.literal: Half lacked complete virtue—a shame before later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Half lacked complete virtue—a shame before later generations.
